function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below are the three files you’ll need to add to the **`zelarhq/nodejs-welcome`** repository.  
After creating them, simply stage, commit, and push the changes.

---

## 1️⃣ Dockerfile

```dockerfile
# Use an official Node runtime as a parent image
FROM node:18-alpine

# Create app directory
WORKDIR /app

# Install app dependencies
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Bundle app source
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app runs on
EXPOSE 3000

# Run the application
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> **Why this Dockerfile?**  
> * `node:18-alpine` is lightweight and contains the latest LTS Node version.  
> * `npm ci` ensures a clean install of production dependencies.  
> * The app is assumed to listen on port **3000** (adjust if your app uses a different port).

---

## 2️⃣ Kubernetes YAML (`k8s.yaml`)

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> **What this does**  
> * Deploys two replicas of your Node.js app.  
> * Exposes the app via a LoadBalancer service on port **80**, forwarding traffic to container port **3000**.  
> * Uses the image that will be pushed to GitHub Container Registry (`ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest`).

---

## 3️⃣ GitHub Actions Workflow (`.github/workflows/docker-image.yml`)

```yaml
name: Build and Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # Check out the repository
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      # Set up Docker Buildx
      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v2

      # Log in to GitHub Container Registry
      - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
        uses: docker/login-action@v2
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Build and push the Docker image
      - name: Build and push Docker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:latest
```

> **How it works**  
> * Triggers on every push to the `main` branch.  
> * Builds the Docker image from the Dockerfile in the repo.  
> * Pushes the image to GitHub Container Registry under the same repository name.  

> **Prerequisites**  
> * No extra secrets are required because the workflow uses the automatically generated `${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`.  
> * Ensure the repository has the **Container Registry** feature enabled (it’s usually on by default).

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & Push

Open a terminal in the root of the cloned repository and run:

```bash
# Stage the new files
git add Dockerfile k8s.yaml .github/workflows/docker-image.yml

# Commit with a descriptive message
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"

# Push to the remote repository
git push origin main
```

Once pushed, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically start building and pushing the Docker image. After the image is available in GHCR, you can deploy it to your cluster using the `k8s.yaml` manifest.

Let me know if you’d like help applying the Kubernetes manifests to a specific cluster or tweaking any of the configurations!
